text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London closed lower in generally quiet post-Easter holiday trade. Initially prices were higher but producer selling soon emerged and pushed prices lower. By the close, spot May was $23 lower at $1,612 per tonne, while July gave up $21 to close at $1,622 per tonne.

There were no fresh fundamental factors to influence prices. Arabica futures in New York bounced back from steep early losses to finish mostly higher in volatile trading. Low levels of consumer coffee stocks in the United States, combined with the prospect of smaller Central American and Colombian crops in 1996/97 aided sentiment.

Moreover, some traders said the latest CFTC commitment of traders data, which showed non-commercial net long positions down to 5,307 lots as of March 25 compared with some 9,000 lots net-commercial longs two weeks ago, indicated there was plenty of room for further speculative buying.

Additionally, a decline in coffee open interest to 37,435 lots as of March 31, from more than 42,000 lots a month ago, may also suggest speculators could beef up their positions. Hence, further price rises are a definite possibility. The increase in certified coffee stocks seems to have come to a halt and after Tuesday's close, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks to be down by 250 60-kg bags to 83,328 bags at the end of March. At the close May was 3.15 cents/lb higher at 194.30 cents/lb, while July added 2.00 cents/lb to close at 176.15 cents/lb.

COLOMBIA - High international coffee prices could help revive Colombia's beleaguered coffee industry and boost production to 13.5 mn 60-kg bags, up from 10.4 mn bags estimated for 1996/97 and compared to 12.9 mn bags produced in 1995/96, Mauritius Cardenas, head of the independent think- thank Fedesarrwollo and son of the National Coffee Growers Federation chief said. He added higher coffee prices would boost the overall growth of Colombia's gross domestic product in 1997, which he said would be close to 4 per cent this year compared to GDP-growth of less than 3 per cent last year.

AUSTRALIA - Australia imported 95,500 bags of coffee in January 1997, 21 per cent more than was imported the same month the previous year. Total imports in calendar year 1996 rose by 3.7 per cent to 845,200 bags. Main suppliers of green coffee in January 1997 were Vietnam (31,100 vs 30,600 bags) and Papua New Guinea (28,000 vs 18,300 bags).

BELGIUM - Belgium imported 166,949 bags of coffee in September 1996, roughly 1 per cent more than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 1.445 mn bags, 4 per cent less than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 7.5 per cent to 2.068 mn bags. Main suppliers of green coffee in January/September 1996 were Ivory Coast (82,100 vs 47,700 bags), Costa Rica (60,800 vs 19,800 bags), Guatemala (50,700 vs 43,600 bags), Brazil (149,600 vs 164,300 bags), Colombia (64,100 vs 50,300 bags) and India (59,500 vs 5,100 bags). The country exported 1.063 mn bags of coffee in January/September 1996, 27 per cent more than was exported the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 7 per cent to 1.204 mn bags.

SWEDEN - Sweden imported 186,788 bags of coffee in September 1996, 2.5 per cent more than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 1.567 mn bags, 24 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 13 per cent to 1.648 mn bags. Main suppliers of green coffee in January/September 1996 were Brazil (312,800 vs 348,300 bags) and Colombia (326,600 vs 283,900 bags). The country exported 166,100 bags of coffee in January/September 1996, 10 per cent more than was exported the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 8.6 per cent to 204,700 bags.

TURKEY - Turkey imported 182,400 bags of coffee in January/June 1996, 110 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 rose by 38 per cent to 184,200 bags. The main supplier of green coffee January/June 1996 was Brazil with 159,600 bags against 67,900 bags the same period in 1995.
